title: Publish a tested Python package
summary: A small, useful Python library or command-line tool, packaged with pyproject.toml, checked by ruff, mypy and pytest in CI, and released to TestPyPI (then PyPI) from a tagged GitHub Actions workflow.
why: Python job postings ask for packaging, testing, typing and CI, and this project shows all four in one place that a reviewer can install with a single command. It proves you can ship code other people depend on, not just code that runs on your laptop.
brief:
Pick a small problem worth packaging: a library that validates or parses something (ISBNs, IBANs, cron expressions, version ranges), a converter (Markdown tables to CSV), or a command-line tool such as `csvstats sales.csv --by region`. Choose something you can finish to a high standard in about 20 hours: small and polished beats large and rough. Check that the name is free on both PyPI and TestPyPI before you start.

Constraints: use a **src layout** and a `pyproject.toml` with a build backend (hatchling, setuptools or uv's). Type the whole public API, run mypy in strict mode, and ship a `py.typed` file so users get your hints. Use ruff for linting and formatting. Test with pytest (fixtures, parametrize, and error cases, not just the happy path) and report coverage. Prefer the standard library; every runtime dependency needs a reason and a version range, not an exact pin. Raise your own exception type for invalid input. If it is a CLI, expose it through `[project.scripts]` with `--help` and meaningful exit codes.

Automate everything: a GitHub Actions workflow runs ruff, mypy and pytest on every push and pull request across at least three Python versions, and branch protection requires it to pass. A second workflow builds the sdist and wheel when you push a version tag and publishes to **TestPyPI** with **trusted publishing**, so no API token ever lives in the repository. Prove the release works by installing it from TestPyPI into a fresh virtual environment and running the README example unchanged. Publishing the same files to PyPI afterwards is optional, but makes a great resume line.

milestones.title: Scope and skeleton
tasks: Write one sentence describing what the package does and who it is for, and check the name on PyPI and TestPyPI
Create the src layout, pyproject.toml with metadata and requires-python, README, LICENSE and .gitignore
Create a venv and install the project in editable mode with a dev extra (pytest, pytest-cov, ruff, mypy)
milestones.doneWhen: In a fresh venv, `python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"` succeeds and `python -c "import yourpkg; print(yourpkg.__version__)"` prints 0.1.0.

milestones.title: Core library with tests
tasks: Implement the public API as small, typed functions or classes with docstrings
Add a custom exception hierarchy for invalid input
Write pytest tests with fixtures and parametrize, covering edge cases and every error path
milestones.doneWhen: `pytest --cov=yourpkg` passes and reports at least 90% line coverage for the core module.

milestones.title: Quality gates
tasks: Configure ruff (lint rules and format) and mypy strict mode in pyproject.toml
Add a py.typed marker file to the package
Add pre-commit hooks for ruff, ruff-format and mypy
milestones.doneWhen: `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .` and `mypy src` all pass, and a commit that adds an unused import is stopped by the pre-commit hook.

milestones.title: Command line and documentation
tasks: If it is a CLI: add a [project.scripts] entry point with argparse, --help and non-zero exit codes on errors, tested with capsys
Write the README: one-sentence pitch, install, quick example, API or CLI usage, development setup
Start a CHANGELOG with a 0.1.0 entry
milestones.doneWhen: After `pip install .` in a fresh venv, the README's quick example works when copied and pasted, and the command's --help prints usage.

milestones.title: Continuous integration
tasks: Add a GitHub Actions workflow with a matrix of three Python versions that runs ruff, mypy and pytest with coverage
Add a CI status badge to the README
Turn on branch protection so main requires the checks to pass
milestones.doneWhen: A pull request shows green checks for all three Python versions, and a pull request with a failing test cannot be merged.

milestones.title: Release to TestPyPI
tasks: Configure trusted publishing for the repository on TestPyPI
Add a release workflow that runs on tags like v0.1.0, builds the sdist and wheel, and publishes them
Tag v0.1.0, then install from TestPyPI into a fresh venv and run the README example
milestones.doneWhen: `python -m pip install -i https://test.pypi.org/simple/ yourpkg` in a fresh venv installs your release (add `--extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/` if it has dependencies) and the documented example runs.

stretch: Publish the same release to PyPI and add a version badge
A documentation site with MkDocs and mkdocstrings, deployed to GitHub Pages
Property-based tests with Hypothesis for the parsing or validation logic
Dependabot or Renovate for dependency and GitHub Actions updates
A 0.2.0 release with a deprecation warning for an API you plan to change, following semantic versioning
rubric: A reviewer should be able to install the package from TestPyPI into a fresh virtual environment and run the README example unchanged
A reviewer should see a src layout and a complete pyproject.toml: metadata, requires-python, dependency ranges, build backend and scripts
A reviewer should find ruff and mypy strict passing in CI on every supported Python version
A reviewer should see tests for edge cases and error paths, not only the happy path, with coverage reported in CI
A reviewer should find no API tokens or passwords in the repository, its history or its workflow files
A reviewer should see a clear public API: typed signatures, docstrings and a custom exception type for invalid input
A reviewer should see semantic versions, a CHANGELOG entry and a git tag for each release
showcase: README sections: one-sentence pitch, install, quick example, API or CLI reference, development setup, contributing, license
Badges for CI status, package version and supported Python versions at the top of the README
Pin the repository on your GitHub profile and link the TestPyPI or PyPI page from your resume
A short write-up of what you learned about packaging and releasing, linked from the README
resumeBullet: Built and published isbnkit, a typed Python library and CLI for validating ISBNs, with 60+ pytest tests (95% coverage), mypy strict and ruff, and a GitHub Actions pipeline that tests Python 3.11 to 3.13 and releases to PyPI from version tags using trusted publishing
interviewTalkingPoints: Why you used a src layout, and the packaging mistake it protects against
How you designed the public API, what you kept private, and how you would make a breaking change under semantic versioning
Why a library declares dependency ranges and does not ship a lock file
How trusted publishing works compared with API tokens, and what triggers a release
What mypy strict caught that tests missed, and the reverse
How you tested the command-line layer separately from the core logic
